title: Balanced Nutrition, Macronutrients, and Daily Dietary Plate
content:
A balanced diet provides essential vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, dietary fiber, and macronutrients required for cellular maintenance and metabolic health. According to evidence-based dietary guidelines, a healthy plate composition should feature:
- Half the Plate: Colorful vegetables and whole fruits (such as leafy greens, cruciferous vegetables, berries, citrus, and carrots), providing vital micronutrients and digestive fiber.
- One Quarter of the Plate: Whole grains (brown rice, whole wheat, oats, quinoa, barley) which deliver sustained complex carbohydrates and prevent sharp blood glucose spikes.
- One Quarter of the Plate: Healthy lean protein sources, including legumes, lentils, beans, tofu, poultry, eggs, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish high in omega-3 fatty acids (like salmon and sardines).
- Healthy Fats in Moderation: Emphasize unsaturated fats such as extra virgin olive oil, avocados, nuts, and seeds while minimizing trans-fats, deep-fried foods, and excessive saturated fats.

Practical guidelines include minimizing added refined sugars (sugary drinks, processed snacks), limiting daily sodium intake to less than 2,300 mg (about one teaspoon of salt), and drinking plenty of clean water instead of sugary beverages. People with specific metabolic concerns (such as diabetes, hypertension, or food allergies) should consult a registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN).
source_name: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health & WHO
